method: The owner pasted real keys into Cursor IDE. Each test sent one short prompt from a new Agent chat, or a prompt asking the Agent to read README.md with its Read tool. A request counts as 'reached' only if Azure (Monitor metrics per deployment, a temporary Log Analytics sink in the first part) or the proxy recorded it. Proxy side: scripts/foundry_claude_proxy.py logs every request it receives, including rejected ones. Client side: scripts/summarize_cursor_agent_log.py over Cursor's local agent-host log. Settings were entered with real keystrokes and then read back from Cursor's saved settings store (not from the screen) before every test from M2 on. UI messages are quoted as shown. Hosts, keys and ids are not published; tunnels and the diagnostic sink were deleted afterwards.

key_validation.check: The key Cursor stored (read from its local encrypted settings) was compared on this machine with the resource's Key2; they were identical. Only the yes/no result was printed; the key itself is not recorded.
key_validation.same_key_direct_calls: 200 on the legacy Azure chat route for the GPT deployments, 200 on /openai/v1/chat/completions and /openai/v1/responses for GPT; Claude 200 on Responses and on /anthropic/v1/messages with x-api-key (key-route-probe.json)

community: F31: staff say the Azure slot needs https://<resource>.openai.azure.com and the exact deployment name; a user confirmed it worked in July 2026. Corroborated by K, L, N and R.
F8: staff say Foundry OpenAI deployments should work through the Azure slot (November 2026). Corroborated by R1 and R2 on a Foundry resource.
F34: a user's 'Network Error' turned out to be a misspelled Base URL. Matches O and the invalid A to H runs: the message is the same for any Base URL Cursor cannot use.
F10, F35, F37: Azure slot failures reported in 2026; staff traced F35 and F37 to Cursor's request building and fixed them in July
F32: staff pointed users at a community proxy for the OpenAI override; S confirms the override reaches a proxy from Cursor's backend
reading: The documented Azure OpenAI slot works. With settings that Cursor actually saved, it ran Agent turns, including a file-tool call, against a classic Azure OpenAI resource (K, L, N) and against a Foundry resource (R1, R2), each confirmed by 200s in Azure. The earlier 'failed in all tests' result came from my UI automation, which never saved the Base URL; an empty Base URL reproduces it exactly (O). Three things do break it: a deployment rate limit too low for Cursor's large prompts (I, J: 429 at 10K TPM), a wrong deployment name (M2), and reasoning models such as GPT-6 Luna, which Foundry refuses because Cursor sends tools over Chat Completions (R3). Claude cannot be reached directly because the slot only speaks the Azure OpenAI Chat Completions route; it works through the translating proxy behind a public tunnel, in the Azure slot (P) and in the OpenAI override (S1, S2). The same proxy fixes Luna by calling the Responses API (Q, S3). The OpenAI override also redirects Cursor's own OpenAI-family models to the proxy and blocks Composer while it is on (S4).

automation_defect.summary: Tests A to H are invalid. The UI automation used to fill Cursor's Base URL and Deployment fields changed what the screen showed but not what Cursor saved, so those tests ran with an empty or stale Base URL.
automation_defect.how_found: Test M1: the Deployment field was changed by the same automation to a name that did not exist; Cursor still answered, Azure logged the request on the old deployment, and Cursor's saved settings still held the old name.
automation_defect.how_confirmed: Test O: an empty saved Base URL, entered deliberately, reproduced the exact A to H signature (Network Error; resource_exhausted four times; about 20 seconds; nothing reaches Azure).
automation_defect.earlier_read_back: The earlier check that 'field values matched the resource' read the on-screen values, which is why it did not catch this.
automation_defect.also_affected: Tests F and F2 and the Premium-round override cases (premium-round.json) were set up the same way. With the override URL unsaved, Cursor would have sent the proxy secret to OpenAI's own API, which explains 'Invalid API key' with no request at the proxy. Test S repeats them with saved settings.
